title: Gamma pool degradation experiment + handoff
content:
Summary:

This note captures an experimental triage and temporary mitigations we ran for a recurring degradation in the 'gamma' dedicated GPU pool during the weekend of 2025-10-31. The symptom set: sudden p95/generation latency jumps, throughput drop of ~30% for ~20–45 minutes, and increased eviction/churn on small-tenant allocations. This file is a handoff to the SRE rotation and eng-serving-runtime for deeper follow-up and permanent remediation work.

Why this exists (short):
- We ran a set of live isolation experiments to validate whether KV-cache amplification or a specific tenant's request patterns were amplifying kernel contention.
- We also exercised autoscaler cooldowns and a temporary eviction tweak to see if we could stabilize tail latency without impacting throughput severely.

Quick timeline (high level):
- 2025-11-01 02:14 UTC: First alert - p95 generation latency > 2.5x baseline.
- 02:18 UTC: On-call (Miguel) confirmed spike; began collecting tracers and rt-metrics (p95/p99, GPU util, queue depth, kv-cache-hit-rate).
- 02:26 UTC: Identified correlated increase in allocation churn and eviction_count metric on gamma-pool nodes.
- 02:33 UTC: Rolled a short experiment: set eviction-threshold to -10% (temporary) to reduce forced migrations.
- 02:37 UTC: Observed partial improvement in queue depth but sustained p99 spikes. Started tenant sampling.
- 02:52 UTC: Isolated one tenant (tenant-id:t-11a3) showing abnormal small-batch behavior and high KV cache miss amplification.
- 03:05 UTC: Applied a temporary CPU-affinity soft-limiter to the offending tenant via runtime flag; latency improved to near baseline, throughput recovered to ~92%.
- 03:30 UTC: Reversed warmup aggressiveness for ephemeral jobs (reduced warmup workers) as a conservative measure.
- 04:15 UTC: Incident declared mitigated; notes captured for follow-up.

Key observations and signals collected (raw):
- GPU util: per-GPU util plateaued but context-switches and SM stalls increased during spikes.
- KV-cache-hit-rate: down ~12% during incident window for certain tenants.
- evictions: eviction_count increased by 3–6x on 3 nodes hosting the noisy tenant.
- autoscaler metrics: scale-out triggers fired but cooldown prevented new slot creation for ~90s longer than expected (mis-set cooldown param in gamma autoscaler config).
- trace sample: 80% of slow requests had an early spike in kernel call time (attention kernel) and repeated KV cache population calls.

Hypotheses tested (and quick result):
1) Noisy-tenant micro-bursting causing KV cache amplification -> supported. Tenant t-11a3 produced many small contexts with cache thrash and frequent KV read misses leading to heavier attention kernel loads.
2) Autoscaler cooldown misconfiguration (too aggressive) prevented fast replenishment of ephemeral slots -> supported. We found cooldown set to 120s in gamma config; intended value was 30s.
3) GPU driver/firmware intermittent slow path -> not supported by our immediate traces (no firmware logs showing interrupts), but keep on bench test list.

Temporary mitigations applied (notes to handoff):
- Tenant soft-throttle: applied a per-tenant soft limiter for t-11a3 (runtime flag: tenant_request_rate_limit=75rps). This is ephemeral; rollback scheduled if customer impact reported.
- Eviction threshold: nudged +10% (less aggressive eviction) to reduce cross-tenant migrations during small bursts. This reduced churn but slightly increased tail for heavy, long-running jobs—monitor.
- Autoscaler cooldown: temporarily set gamma autoscaler cooldown back to 30s (config change id: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/987).
- Warmup throttling: reduce ephemeral warmup parallelism to limit cache-population storms.

Playbook draft (recommended order for on-call):
1) Confirm signal: p95 > 2x baseline and eviction_count spike on pool nodes.
2) Snapshot metrics for affected nodes (store snapshot id in incident ticket).
3) Tenant Sampling: run tenant-scan script (utils/tenant-probe.sh) for top-k allocations by churn.
4) If a single tenant is dominant: apply per-tenant soft-throttle and observe 5–15 minutes.
5) If multisource: increase eviction threshold conservatively, monitor queue depth and sm_stalls.
6) Autoscaler check: ensure cooldown isn't preventing corrective scaling. If cooldown > 60s, reduce to 30s temporarily.
7) If mitigation fails after 30m: failover traffic to fallback pool (region/capacity-tier) and engage runtime on-call for a safe rollback.

Commands & snippets used during triage (for handoff):
- Gather top-tenant churn: ./tools/top_tenant_churn --pool gamma --window 10m --output csv
- Node snapshot: curl http://obs-api/internal/snapshots?pool=gamma&since=2025-11-01T01:50Z -o gamma-snap-20251101.json
- Apply soft throttle: infractl set-tenant -p gamma -t t-11a3 --rate 75
- Change autoscaler cooldown: kubectl apply -f gamma-autoscaler-patch.yaml (see PR #987 for rollback instructions)

Open questions / unknowns (needs follow-up):
- Why did t-11a3 switch to the small-batch pattern during the weekend? Customer-side release or client-side retries? Need Solutions Eng to contact account team.
- Are there underlying kernel scheduling pathologies for a particular model family when KV cache miss rates spike? Need runtime bench with a synthetic reproducer.
- Is eviction threshold nudging safe long-term? We reduced migrations but may allow long-lived cache pollution for heavy tenants. Need simulation in the autoscaler test harness.

Post-incident actions (owners & suggested due dates):
- INF-2342: Create synthetic reproducer for t-11a3 pattern and test on bench (owner: Jonah Lee, due: 2025-11-14).
- Runtime PR: add tenant-level per-request histogram export to help identify micro-burst patterns (owner: Rina Patel, PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1012, due: 2025-11-10).
- Config audit: review all autoscaler cooldown values across pools and add an automated alert if cooldown > 60s (owner: Priya Rao, due: 2025-11-12).
- Perf test: run GPU driver stress job on gamma-config nodes to look for firmware-related stalls (owner: Platform Eng rotation, due: 2025-11-20).

Customer / business notes:
- There is one affected tenant that may see a soft-rate limit applied briefly. Solutions Eng to proactively reach out and explain the incident and temporary throttling if customer queries appear.
- No SLA credit action expected yet; we will escalate to legal/ops if customer escalates.

Retention & monitoring changes suggested:
- Add tenant-level eviction_count alert when a single tenant accounts for > 50% of evictions in 5m window.
- New dashboard: gamma-pool microburst panel (top 10 tenants by churn, kv_cache_hit_rate, sm_stalls).

Notes to the next on-call (short TL;DR):
- If you see p95 spikes + eviction churn, run tenant-scan. If single tenant dominates, apply soft-throttle; if multisource, nudge eviction and check autoscaler cooldown. If unstable after 30m, fail traffic to fallback pool.
- Slack channel: #sre-gamma-pool-thread. Incident ticket: JIRA INF-2342.

Appendix (handy links & raw outputs):
- Raw metric snapshot: gamma-snap-20251101.json (attached to INF-2342)
- Top tenant churn CSV: top-churn-gamma-20251101.csv
- PR for cooldown rollback: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/987

Free-form notes / thoughts to keep in doc (notes-to-self style):
- We should consider moving some tenants to a burst-isolated class where small-batch work is scheduled on a subset of nodes that tolerate KV churn (tradeoff: lower global cache efficiency, higher isolation).
- Long term, a tenant QoS classification at admission time could prevent noisy micro-bursts from degrading other tenants: 'small-batch', 'long-run', 'interactive'.
- Watch out: warming throttles reduce cache pollution but may increase cold-start latency for legitimate interactive requests (tradeoff).
- Document the tenant sampling script and make it accessible from the SRE runbook quick-links.

End of note. Handoff: assigned to on-call rotation week starting 2025-11-08. Please add any additional follow-up items as children of INF-2342.
